text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Scottish/Australian biscuit maker WILLIAM ARNOTT, who started manufacturing in Newcastle before opening a factory in Sydney, was born in 1827.
The first Principal of Sydney's Church of England Grammar School for Girls, EDITH BADHAM, was born in 1853. It reportedly taught only boating, SHAKESPEARE and The Bible.
American lyricist IRA GERSHWIN, who wrote hits with his brother GEORGE, was born in 1896. Successes included "Lady Be Good" and "I Got Rhythm".
American jazz pianist and composer DAVE BRUBECK, who had a hit with "Take Five", was born in 1920.

British singer, songwriter, producer and owner of record company U.K. Records, JONATHAN KING (real first name KENNETH) was born in 1944. He wrote his first hit "Everyone's Gone To The Moon" in 1965. He wrote for pop magazines, produced the first album for 'Genesis' and supported and discovered the group '10CC'. In 1975 he had a hit with "Una Paloma Blanca". He was a presenter on UK TV in the early eighties, in particular the BBC programme "Entertainment USA".
United States drummer with 'Looking Glass' JEFF GROB was born in 1950.
** EVENTS **
1774 : Austria became the first nation to establish a
state education system.
1911 : Mongolia was declared a Russian protectorate.
1921 : Ireland was split in two. The 26 southern states
were granted independence from Britain, becoming the Irish Free State. In the North six of the eight Protestant-majority counties of Ulster remained part of the United Kingdom.
1926 : French impressionist painter CLAUDE MONET died at
the age of 86. MONET founded the impressionist movement with friends RENOIR, PISSARO and SISLEY. MONET's favourite subject for his paintings was the lily pond in his garden at Giverny.
1942 : The Church of England in the United Kingdom ruled
that it no longer required women to wear hats in church. Women could bare their heads just like men.
1963 : London model CHRISTINE KEELER was sentenced to

nine months imprisonment for perjury and conspiracy to pervert the course of justice. The 21-year-old admitted lying when she concealed the fact that two men were hiding in her bedroom when an ex-boyfriend assaulted her. She was the protege of DR STEPHEN WARD, who ran a high-society sex ring. She was linked with JOHN PROFUMO, the Minister for War.
1969 : An 18-year-old black youth was murdered in front

of the stage while 'The Rolling Stones' performed at a free concert at Altamont Speedway in California. MEREDITH HUNTER was stabbed to death by Hell's Angels bikers when he pulled out a gun during a scuffle. "The Stones' had hired the US bikers as security guards after using their tamer British counterparts in the UK. This was the final performance of their US tour and after hurriedly finishing their remaining numbers they escaped in a helicopter.
1973 : In Buenos Aires Peronists launched a campaign to

regain the Falklands from Britain. The campaign eventually led to the Falklands War. Argentina invaded and occupied the islands in April 1982. A British force was dispatched and after two months of fighting and the loss of one thousand lives the islands were returned to British rule.
1981 : Australia's ROBERT DE CASTELLA won the Fukuoka
marathon in two hours, eight minutes and 18 seconds.
1988 : American rock 'n' roll singer ROY ORBISON died of
a heart attack at the age of 52.
1990 : An Italian military aircraft crashed into a
secondary school near Bologna, killing 12 and injuring 65.
1990 : SADDAM HUSSEIN announced that the 3400 foreign
hostages held in Iraq since the invasion of Kuwait were free to leave.
1991 : French President FRANCOIS MITTERRAND honoured the

victorious French Davis Cup tennis team, who won the trophy after 59 years. The hero of the day was the team coach YANNICK NOAH. NOAH was quoted as saying "Guy was happy, I was happy, the team was happy, the crowd was happy, everybody was happy. There is just one word to describe it all - happiness".
1994 : Freight company MAYNE NICKLESS was fined a toal of
7.7 million dollars by the Federal Court, for price fixing and collusion over a period of about 20 years.
